from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Intuitive Hook: The Cocktail Party Effect", 
                          ["Transformers use selective focus like a party.", 
                           "Humans filter noise to hear one speaker.", 
                           "Models filter relevant tokens from a sequence."])

        # Animation Setup
        # Create representation of people talking
        people = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.3, color=BLUE).add(Dot(radius=0.05)) for _ in range(6)])
        for i, p in enumerate(people):
            self.place_at_grid(p, ["B2", "B4", "C3", "D2", "D4", "E3"][i])
        
        focus_person = Circle(radius=0.4, color=YELLOW).add(Dot(radius=0.08, color=YELLOW))
        self.place_at_grid(focus_person, "C5")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.play(FadeIn(people), FadeIn(focus_person))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        # Simulate background noise
        noise_waves = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=0.4, angle=PI/2, color=BLUE_D).move_to(p.get_center()) for p in people])
        self.play(Create(noise_waves), run_time=1.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        # Highlight focus and fade noise
        self.play(
            FadeOut(noise_waves),
            focus_person.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
            people.animate.set_opacity(0.3),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Attention Scores (Softmax)", 
                          ["Attention scores determine token relevance.", 
                           "High scores mean bright connections.", 
                           "Softmax maps similarity to importance."])
        
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Represent scores as bars of different heights.
        bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.5, height=h, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE)
            for h in [1.5, 0.5, 2.0, 0.8]
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(bars, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(bars))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(0.5)
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(1)
        # Highlight highest score bar with color #FF00FF.
        self.play(bars[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_opacity(0.5)
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        # Apply Softmax transformation to normalize bars to sum 1.
        new_heights = [0.2, 0.1, 0.5, 0.2]
        new_bars = VGroup(*[
            Rectangle(width=0.5, height=h*4, fill_opacity=0.8, color=BLUE if i!=2 else "#FF00FF")
            for i, h in enumerate(new_heights)
        ]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(new_bars, "B2", "D5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Transform(bars, new_bars))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Attention combines Q, K, and V vectors.",
            "We calculate weights via dot products.",
            "Values are summed based on these weights.",
            "Result: A context-aware representation.",
            "The formula represents a weighted mix."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Mathematical Workflow", lecture_lines)

        # Define color scheme
        Q_COLOR = BLUE
        K_COLOR = GREEN
        V_COLOR = YELLOW

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Attention combines Q, K, and V vectors.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        q_rect = Rectangle(width=1, height=2, color=Q_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        k_rect = Rectangle(width=1, height=2, color=K_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        v_rect = Rectangle(width=1, height=2, color=V_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.5)
        
        q_label = Text("Q", color=Q_COLOR).next_to(q_rect, UP)
        k_label = Text("K", color=K_COLOR).next_to(k_rect, UP)
        v_label = Text("V", color=V_COLOR).next_to(v_rect, UP)
        
        group = VGroup(q_rect, k_rect, v_rect, q_label, k_label, v_label)
        self.place_in_area(group, "A1", "C6", scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # We calculate weights via dot products.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(ORANGE)
        dot_product_text = MathTex("Q \\cdot K^T", color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_product_text, "D3")
        self.play(Write(dot_product_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Values are summed based on these weights.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        sum_text = MathTex("\\sum (Weights \\cdot V)", color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_text, "D4")
        self.play(Write(sum_text))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Result: A context-aware representation.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(PURPLE)
        res_rect = Rectangle(width=2, height=1, color=PURPLE, fill_opacity=0.7)
        res_label = Text("Context-Aware\nOutput", font_size=20, color=PURPLE).move_to(res_rect)
        res_group = VGroup(res_rect, res_label)
        self.place_at_grid(res_group, "E4")
        self.play(FadeIn(res_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The formula represents a weighted mix.
        self.lecture[4].set_color(RED)
        formula = MathTex("Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(\\frac{QK^T}{\\sqrt{d_k}})V", font_size=30, color=RED)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "F1", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Transformers enable massive parallel processing.", "RNNs read one word at a time.", "Attention processes the entire sequence simultaneously."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary: Why Transformers Rule", lecture_lines)
        self.lecture.set_opacity(0)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_opacity(1)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Parallel processing icon/blocks
        blocks = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5) for _ in range(4)])
        blocks.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(blocks, 'B2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Create(blocks), Write(self.lecture[0]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        # RNN icon (one block)
        rnn_block = Square(side_length=0.5, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(rnn_block, 'E2', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(rnn_block), Write(self.lecture[1]))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_opacity(1)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Text
        text = Text("Transformers are powerful", font_size=36, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(text, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(text), Write(self.lecture[2]))

outline.topic: The Attention Mechanism: How Transformers Read
outline.target_audience: University students with basic programming/math background

sections.title: The Intuitive Hook: The Cocktail Party Effect
sections.content: Introduce the concept of 'selective focus'. Just as humans filter out background noise to listen to one speaker, models need to filter relevant tokens from a sequence.
sections.example: Imagine a crowded party. You ignore the background chatter but immediately 'attend' to your name being called across the room.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
sections.content: Explain the Q, K, and V vectors using a database analogy. Define Q (what I'm looking for), K (what I have to offer), and V (the content I provide). Pre-requisite: Dot product as a measure of similarity.
sections.example: A library search: Your search term is the 'Query'. The book labels are the 'Keys'. The information inside the book is the 'Value'.

sections.title: Visualizing Attention Scores (Softmax)
sections.content: Explain how the dot product of Q and K determines relevance. Use a heatmap animation to show how high-relevance tokens get 'bright' and low-relevance ones fade.
sections.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired', the word 'it' has a high attention score (bright connection) to 'animal' but a low score to 'street'.

sections.title: The Mathematical Workflow
sections.content: Synthesize the components into the formula: Attention(Q, K, V) = softmax(QK^T / sqrt(dk))V. Visualize this as a weighted sum of values, where weights are determined by the alignment between Q and K.
sections.example: Think of it as a weighted recipe: The Query decides the importance of each ingredient (Key), and we mix the flavors (Values) based on those importance weights.

sections.title: Summary: Why Transformers Rule
sections.content: Conclude by highlighting 'Parallelization'. Unlike RNNs that read one word at a time, Attention processes all words simultaneously, allowing for the massive scale of modern LLMs.
sections.example: An RNN is like reading a book through a pinhole; a Transformer is like taking a high-speed photograph of the entire page at once.
